match.reason: Neither bank point covers flexible or remote work or how it can balance or blur work and life; one lists types of paid and unpaid work and the other covers why people work, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Flexible and remote work
card: Working away from the employer's workplace, often from home, using a computer and the internet.
Having some choice over when or how much you work, such as part-time hours or starting and finishing at different times.
More people now work this way. It can help them balance work with life outside work, such as caring for family, study or sport. It can also save time spent travelling to work.
It can also blur the line between work and home life. A worker may answer messages late at night or find it hard to switch off.
draft.remember: Flexible and remote work can help balance life and work, but it can also blur the line between them.

a.q: Sam works from home on a laptop and can choose his start time each day. What is one benefit this may give him?
opts: It can help him balance work with life outside work
It means he will never need to answer work messages
It makes his work and home life become the same thing
It means his employer no longer needs to pay him
a.why: Choosing where and when to work can make it easier to fit in family, study or sport. The other options say too much: the card says only that it can help, and it can also blur the line between work and home.
a.clue: Think about fitting work around life outside work.

b.q: Priya works from home for a design firm. She now often replies to emails at 10 pm and finds it hard to stop thinking about work. Which problem does this show?
opts: The line between work and home life has become blurred
She has moved from a service job to a factory job
Her work is flexible only because she works part-time
She has lost the chance to balance work with life
b.why: Working from home can make it hard to separate work time from personal time, which is what Priya is finding. Flexible and remote work can still help balance work and life in other ways, so she has not lost the chance to do so.
b.clue: Look at the time she answers emails and how she feels afterwards.

a.best: It can help him balance work with life outside work

b.best: The line between work and home life has become blurred

problems.detail: The right option is the only one hedged with 'can'. The others use 'means' or 'makes', and one says 'never', so a student could pick it by its qualifier alone.
The clue 'Think about fitting work around life outside work' almost restates the right option, which gives the answer away.
